frequency_question: How often does the U.S. Treasury execute major banking sanctions against systemically important foreign lenders when violations are identified and statutory authority is present?
membership_rule: Includes executive actions targeting Tier-1 foreign commercial banks for sanctions breaches under specific secondary sanction authorities; excludes advisory warnings, diplomatic demarches, or penalties solely against minor shell companies/tier-3 entities.

cases.name: Bank of Kunlun (Iran secondary sanctions designation)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major historical enforcement events involving systemically significant or major foreign banks for severe sanctions evasion.
known_gaps: Does not account for unpublicized waivers or internal executive deliberations that aborted before formal Treasury designation.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 documented major enforcement actions against systemically relevant institutions where the executive demonstrated will and capability.
validity_reason: Tied to the longevity of current U.S. statutory frameworks (CAATSA, NDAA provisions) and executive enforcement posture, which resets with presidential administrations.
